gen-dafont-azonix-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Azonix is wide, commanding and a touch slow to knit back together. Pilcrow Rounded then settles in with big counters, tight letter spacing and curves left open, so paragraphs of it feel warm and snug rather than stiff.
gen-dafont-azonix-fs-quicksand: Quicksand brings friendly, tall, bulb-round lowercase and terminals that stop well short of the stem. Quicksand stays quiet while Azonix, wide and commanding, earns its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-blockletter-fs-alpino: A tall, squat-bellied midsection defines the precise Blockletter. But Alpino keeps things cozy and casual, its tall body making ascenders look short and its curve endings staying well apart.
gen-dafont-blockletter-fs-hind: Blockletter is precise and modern, with a tall, squat-bellied midsection. Hind's sans lowercase nearly matches its capitals and its strokes run taut as drawn string, giving the heading's pencil-line build a steady partner.
gen-dafont-blockletter-fs-nunito: Blockletter draws each glyph as a ribbon of constant width, precise and modern, with a tall squat midsection. Blockletter makes the statement; Nunito, all big round bowls, does the friendly talking.
gen-dafont-blockletter-fs-pilcrow-rounde: Pilcrow Rounded is warm sans-serif with big counters and curves that refuse to close. Pilcrow Rounded softens what Blockletter keeps pencil-precise, and that tension is the whole appeal.
gen-dafont-blockletter-fs-quicksand: Sharp pencil lines, soft glass bulbs: Blockletter carries the precision while Quicksand rounds out the lowercase with open terminals. Give Blockletter the big sizes and let Quicksand stay modest.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-alpino: Bloody comes on commanding, its big round lowercase bowls giving the heading real presence over Alpino. Alpino, cozy and casual sans-serif with tight spacing, supplies the friendly counterweight.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-familjen-grotesk: Bloody commands attention with big round lowercase bowls, loud and unmistakably bloody, and it never asks to be subtle. Familjen Grotesk, a lively plain sans with unfinished bowls, does the explaining.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-hind: Big round lowercase bowls give Bloody its loud, commanding face, instantly bloody in mood. And Hind, a sans with strokes taut as drawn string, gives that loudness a steady, professional counterpart.
